title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang — back before a single hearing
summary: A catch-up episode after a few days off: Nvidia's board brings Jensen Huang back before Congress has heard from him, Anthropic's interviews with 58 customers find hiring that never happened rather than layoffs, Claude Ship lets an agent approve pull requests under a team-written policy, and Anthropic researchers find most unlearning methods hide hazardous knowledge instead of removing it. Plus the Lean community certifying the Riemann proof, an unchecked Claude proof that VP is not VNP, OpenAI's proposed perplexity limit, the rest of November 21-24, and an 1808 sketchbook identified in twenty-two minutes.

topics: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang (23 Nov 2026): CEO, president and director; Latent Space reports unanimous board vote citing input from senior US officials, independent directors' investigation continuing, new board committee for national security and export control; TechCrunch reports Trump called into the board meeting, Politico quotes White House spokesman Steve Cheung that the President was 'totally involved'; at 24 Nov all-hands (WSJ via TechCrunch) Huang thanked the administration for quick access to intelligence that helped the board judge national-security risk low, said he is in therapy; told staff (CNBC via TechCrunch) succession planning would create unnecessary hierarchy; ~60 direct reports, five executive officers; Kress back to CFO after 12 days as interim; open letter 200,000+ signatures incl. ~10,000 current employees; Senate Banking hearing 3 Dec, three House committees 1 Dec; Semafor via TechCrunch: Megaspeed headed for Commerce Entity List; stock up 30%+ Monday, down 7%+ Tuesday midday. Unresolved: Ada calls the board's reversal 'a veto with extra steps'; Alan says the reinstatement fixed the stock, not the risk.

Anthropic 'Working with AI' (Wilmers, Massenkoff, McCrory; 23 Nov 2026): 66 interviews at 58 US enterprise customers, not representative, self-reported value; five companies pushed out AI non-adopters, two saw a position eliminated by automation, ten hiring more, two-thirds hiring less ('We may not be firing, but we're not hiring'); nine cut contractors, many offshore (one finance firm >100 offshore contractors); highest-value uses required reorganization; law firm pairing juniors with seniors to mark up AI drafts; Paul David's electrified mills as the frame. Alan: a vendor saying reorganize around its product; Ada: both can be true.

Claude Ship (Anthropic, 23 Nov 2026): Code Review (GA) + PR Steward (beta, designed never to approve/merge, comments what it changed and how to undo) + Claude Approvals (beta, team-written policy file on the default branch, 'a smarter CODEOWNERS file', observe-only mode recommended first); Claude Code team merged PRs more than doubled June-September with reverted share down 40%+; token billing with spend limits; not available with ZDR, HIPAA configuration or customer-managed keys. Open question raised on air: what happens when a PR edits the policy file.

Anthropic Alignment Science 'Returning to the Neuron Basis' Parts 1-2 (23 Nov 2026, Anthropic Fellows): neurons add two unrelated concepts at once in ~1% or fewer of sampled cases; 23 WMDP-cyber unlearned models (20 external, 3 K-FADE), cloze scoring shows 14 of 23 still rank the correct answer first for most facts the original knew; restoring a few dozen of ~460,000 neurons recovers about half or more of lost facts in several methods; best-scoring methods' most-changed neurons fire 20-100x harder on cyber text — a backdoor-like tripwire; authors argue true post-hoc removal may be impossible in a generalizing way and favor isolating knowledge during training; caveat: open-weight models, mostly short fine-tunes.

dives.story: Anthropic's finding that unlearning hides rather than removes knowledge
dives.why_it_matters: Anyone relying on unlearning as a safety or compliance claim learns that WMDP-style multiple-choice scores can certify forgetting that didn't happen.

concepts_taught: why unlearning benchmarks can certify forgetting that didn't happen: multiple-choice accuracy at chance while cloze scoring still ranks the right answer first, and best-scoring methods implementing a backdoor-like tripwire (a few neurons firing 20-100x on forget-domain text to scramble computation) rather than removal
